scope: tools/playthrough.mjs run end to end on the post-integration tree. The shared-kit integration was rebuilt onto this main rather than merged, and playthrough was the one functional suite never re-run against the result. This closes that gap. It is a headless-Chromium behavioural run, not a device claim.
why_it_was_outstanding: The integration branch swapped the four static servers onto .kit/lib/browser/serve.mjs. playthrough.mjs is one of the four callers, so the swap is on its path, and it had only been run on the pre-integration tree. It takes about an hour on this rig; an earlier attempt was killed by a 20-minute cap after three of five paths, which reads exactly like a hang and is not one.

tree.build: node build.mjs --dev, not rebuilt during the run

limits: Five distinct endings were reached and every path reported ok. This says the integrated tree still runs the game to completion in headless Chromium; it says nothing about rendering, feel, or any real device. Blocker B1 stands.
